result.summary:
As 文献员 for seed 807 round 1, I read rules.md and the four literature prompts (L1-L4) at the end of analysis.md, which target: (L1) price/market-cap *level* variance vs return variance and the drift term it mixes in, plus overnight/intraday/realized-variance decomposition and low-vol anomalies in A-shares; (L2) peer-group demeaning vs regression-residual neutralization and the LimitWidth bucketing field; (L3, flagged most important) the scale contamination (1/sd(X)) inherent in using a rolling regression slope as a cross-sectional factor, plus volume-volatility comovement (mixture-of-distributions hypothesis); (L4) float-share-change events (lockup unlocks, SEOs, buybacks, share pledges) and whether literature has a ready way to turn them into a continuous cross-sectional factor.

I loaded WebSearch/WebFetch via ToolSearch and ran roughly 25 searches plus several WebFetch calls to confirm exact titles, authors, dates and venues, discarding sources I could not date confidently before 2023-08-08 (e.g. a 2025 NYU thesis, a 2024 China Finance Review International SEO paper, an Ehsani-Harvey-Li journal version dated 2023 FAJ issue — kept only its Nov-2021 SSRN working-paper form) and discarding sources whose title/authors I could not pin down (an unconfirmed China private-placement-unlock paper, an unconfirmed HK IPO lock-in study, a date-uncertain Chinese IVOL-by-sampling-frequency working paper).

For each L-item I wrote (in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C08/partura/s807/r1/lit.md): concrete literature-documented processing methods translated into the project's own operator language, each tied to a specific citation, e.g. Rogers-Satchell (1991) / Yang-Zhang (2000) drift-independent OHLC variance construction as a replacement for naive ts_var on price/cap levels; Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard (2004) bipower-variation continuous/jump split as a way to separate the "float-share-jump" component from smooth daily variance; Lou-Polk-Skouras (2019 JFE) overnight-vs-intraday return decomposition; Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang (2006 JF) and Robeco/Blitz (2021) on idiosyncratic/low-volatility anomalies in China; Asness-Porter-Stevens (2000) and DGTW (1997) on industry/characteristic-bucket demeaning, with Ehsani-Harvey-Li (2021) flagging that long-only portfolios may NOT benefit from full sector-neutralization (a caution against assuming BoardCode-bucket is automatically better than LimitWidth-bucket); Wan et al. (2015 PLOS ONE) and Qi (2023-06 PLOS ONE, confirmed published just before the 2023-08-08 cutoff) on China's price-limit mechanics showing the limit's informational content is event-level (hitting the limit), not a static per-stock bucket label; Frazzini-Pedersen's (2014 JFE) own BAB construction (shrinkage + rank, not raw beta) and Novy-Marx & Velikov's (2018 WP / 2022 JFE) proof that regression-beta is predictably biased by scale/volatility, directly mirroring the cross_regbeta "1/sd(X)" diagnosis, which is the literature basis for the paper's proposed cross_corr ablation (R-D); Clark (1973)/Tauchen-Pitts (1983)/Harris (1987)/Richardson-Smith (1994) mixture-of-distributions-hypothesis papers on volume-volatility comovement; and for L4, Liao-Liu-Wang (2011 Financial Management) on split-share lockup-expiration CARs (effect front-loaded before the unlock date), Gan-Bian-Wu-Cohen (2017) on buyback announcement effects (opposite sign/direction from unlocks — argues for using a *signed* float-share delta rather than ts_var), and Li-Liu-Scott (2018) on share pledges showing the pledge-crash-risk relationship is not settled in the literature. I explicitly reported, per the task's "don't fabricate" instruction, that no paper was found giving a ready-made way to turn a discrete corporate event into an always-on continuous cross-sectional factor (only event-window CAR methodology or discrete index-provider rebalance triggers exist), so that sub-question of L4 is marked as "not found" rather than answered speculatively.

Every source in lit.md carries title, author(s), year-month, venue/source, link, and a verified:true/false flag (true only when I actually saw it in a search result or fetched page); unconfirmed or date-uncertain candidates are listed separately under "搜到但未核实/弃用" in each section rather than cited as fact. No other files were modified; I did not touch missions.yaml, corr files, loc files, or any file outside this role's assignment, per rules.md §5.
